I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the most steady way for me to farm: I know how to do it, the grain has a reliable outlet, and I can manage it at my age without making the year too complicated. I will not split too much land into many small crops, because that adds labor, seed choices, and marketing trouble. I would rather do the familiar grain rotation well than chase higher-risk crops.

For the wheat, I will focus on a solid stand, base fertilizer, one good watering at jointing and another around grain filling if water allows, and careful weed and disease control. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize on the same land so I do not lose moisture or time. For maize, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer early with some topdressing at the big-leaf stage, water only when really needed, and keep pest sprays limited to what is necessary. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me than deep ploughing every season, and it fits this wheat-maize rotation.
